title: Implement Geofencing Security for Stream Ingress
description: StreamPulse Nexus needs a new security feature to comply with content licensing agreements for its enterprise clients. The feature, Geofencing, will restrict where streams can be published from, based on the publisher's country. This is a critical, high-priority feature that must be integrated carefully into the existing authentication and orchestration flows. The implementation will be staged over three development sessions to ensure stability and proper integration.

project_spec.name: StreamPulse Nexus
project_spec.description:
StreamPulse Nexus is a component-based networking platform that powers large-scale, interactive entertainment streams (e-sports tournaments, live concerts, virtual festivals) with carrier-grade reliability. Each node in the system orchestrates media packets, chat traffic, game telemetry, and real-time audience interactions while continuously monitoring health, balancing load, and enforcing zero-trust security—creating a seamless, high-energy experience for millions of concurrent viewers.

Built from loosely-coupled components, the project divides networking concerns (ingress, egress, edge caching, transcoding, analytics, alerting, backup/recovery) into swappable runtime modules. Observer and Event-Driven patterns let media routers broadcast state changes to dashboards, while the Command and Chain-of-Responsibility patterns coordinate disaster-recovery commands that cascade through clusters. Strategy pattern injects custom load-balancing algorithms that adapt to show formats (e.g., battle-royale vs. DJ set) and real-time audience heat maps. This architecture lets entertainment engineers remix new interactive features—like synchronized AR effects or timed trivia—without rewriting the core network stack.

Entertainment value is amplified through real-time performance metrics that drive on-screen overlays, live leaderboards, and audience achievements. Log aggregation feeds machine-learning models that surface highlight reels automatically, turning operational telemetry into compelling content. Automated backup and recovery guarantee that captured footage and user engagements remain safe, ready for instant replay or post-event VOD monetization.
dependencies: ws (low-level WebSocket server for media control)
Kubernetes (or K8s-lite like k3s) for cluster orchestration
Envoy or NGINX for edge load balancing
MinIO or AWS S3 SDK (backup/recovery blobs)
OWASP ZAP CLI or Snyk (security scanning pipeline)
